A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 41-page versions of the same work. The text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite figure renumbering and subsection reordering.

before.justification: V2 reports original routing experiments on RouterBench, SPROUT, and Open LLM Leaderboard v2 in Section 4, with additional robustness, ablation, and query-type results in Appendix C.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results, including Table 1 and the supplementary experiments in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Section 2 retain the same ANNS feature estimation, initial random routing, one-time dual optimization, and subsequent routing using learned weights. No method component or objective changes.

E1.justification: The three benchmarks, their constituent tasks, and the evaluated query-order, deployment, budget, noise, and distribution-shift scenarios remain unchanged. V3's additional main-text plots repeat existing appendix evaluations.

E2.justification: The baseline definitions and plotted comparison series remain unchanged. V3 Figure 13 removes spurious Roberta_Perf and Roberta_Cost legend entries from v2 Figure 11 without removing any curves. Both Roberta baselines remain evaluated in Table 1 and other corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Data splits, metrics, budgets, deployment configurations, and sensitivity-sweep settings are retained. The historical-data-size and candidate-count protocols described more prominently in v3 were already specified in v2 Appendix C.6; no replacement experimental settings are stated.

E4.justification: V3 Figures 7–8 redisplay RouterBench sensitivity results already present in v2 Figures 11–12. The historical-data-size discussion moves from C.6 to C.5. The embedding, parameter, noise/OOD, query-order, and query-type analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 100 random query-order trials, 100 random-budget-split runs, 10 deployment-sampling repetitions, and the same error-bar reporting. No run-count, seed, or uncertainty-estimation changes are documented.

E6.justification: Matched tables, plotted trajectories, and heatmap values are unchanged, including Tables 1, 7, and 8. V3's new main-text figures repeat existing results; the historical-data-size figure changes its legend rather than its underlying numerical series.

T1.justification: The optimization formulations, Assumption 1, Theorem 1, auxiliary lemmas, and Appendix B proofs are unchanged. Appendix D also retains the same proposed traffic-capacity constraint.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same training-free online-routing novelty claim, near-optimal competitive guarantee, and empirical claims across three benchmarks and eight baselines.

C2.justification: The expanded main-text sensitivity discussion repeats interpretations already in v2's appendix. Parameter-effect explanations, robustness interpretations, and the traffic/load-balancing limitations in Section 5 and Appendix D remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 deletes the historical-data-size experiment's statement that training-based baselines use the full historical dataset, accompanying the legend correction. Reference 54 adds an explicit OpenHermes-2.5 dataset URL. Other implementation, hardware, and code-access disclosures remain unchanged; no retraining is established.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain the same, including Appendix E. Numerous references receive publication, author, title, or URL updates, but these are bibliographic revisions rather than additions to the related research.

P1.justification: Section 4.1 expands a brief appendix pointer into a paragraph summarizing existing sensitivity results. Appendix C.5 and C.6 exchange order, and references and cross-references are updated. The broader narrative remains substantially verbatim.

P2.justification: V3 adds two main-text figures reproducing existing RouterBench panels, renumbers appendix figures, and relocates Tables 7–8 through reflow. It also corrects v2 Figure 11's mismatched nine-entry legend to the seven plotted series in v3 Figure 13, correctly identifying the red-star series as Ours.

improvement.justification: V3 corrects a misleading legend that labeled the leading red-star series Roberta_Perf in v2 Figure 11, now correctly labeled Ours in Figure 13, and removes the associated inconsistent training-baseline statement. Bringing existing sensitivity evidence into the main text also improves accessibility. These are useful gains in clarity and internal consistency, while the method, theory, and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
